subject: pharmacology
title: Anticholinesterases and myasthenia gravis

steps.tx: Anticholinesterases stop acetylcholine breakdown, so transmitter accumulates at muscarinic, nicotinic and central synapses together. Carbamates such as **neostigmine** carbamylate the enzyme reversibly for hours of action. **Organophosphates** phosphorylate the enzyme almost irreversibly until ageing closes the reactivation window. The same mechanism relieves myasthenia and poisons farm workers exposed to insecticides. The synapse diagram shows normal and blocked transmission side by side for revision.
steps.say: These drugs are cholinergic because they stop acetylcholine breakdown at every cholinergic synapse in body. Carbamates are reversible because they block the enzyme reversibly for hours of action only. Organophosphates are persistent because they block almost permanently until ageing occurs in enzyme. Myasthenia benefit and insecticide poisoning are linked because they share one mechanism in common.

vis.caption: Anticholinesterases block AChE, causing acetylcholine accumulation and intensified transmission

steps.tx: Physostigmine crosses into the brain and reverses central anticholinergic delirium, while quaternary agents stay peripheral by design. **Pyridostigmine** gives longer smoother relief in myasthenia gravis and suits oral maintenance therapy. **Neostigmine** reverses muscle blockade after surgery and treats myasthenia parenterally when swallowing fails. Donepezil raises central cholinergic tone modestly in Alzheimer disease over months. The compare panel separates peripheral from central agents by brain entry.
steps.say: Physostigmine is central because it enters the brain and reverses anticholinergic delirium in patients. Pyridostigmine is peripheral because it stays peripheral and suits myasthenia maintenance therapy well. Neostigmine is useful because it reverses surgical muscle blockade in recovery rooms after anaesthesia. Donepezil is central because it raises central tone modestly in Alzheimer disease over months.

steps.tx: Antibodies destroy postsynaptic receptors in **myasthenia gravis**, causing fatigable weakness worst in evenings with ptosis and diplopia. Pyridostigmine relieves symptoms without changing immunity, so thymectomy and immunotherapy modify the disease itself. Bulbar and respiratory failure define crisis that intensive care supports urgently. Excess drug causes **cholinergic crisis** with fasciculations, salivation and weakness that mimics worsening disease. The table separates the two crises by secretions, pupils and muscle signs.
steps.say: Myasthenia antibodies destroy receptors and cause fatigable evening weakness. Ptosis and diplopia are classic early signs in patients. Pyridostigmine relieves symptoms without changing immunity at all. Excess drug causes cholinergic crisis mimicking worsening disease closely.

steps.tx: Organophosphate poisoning floods every synapse: salivation, miosis, bronchospasm and diarrhoea sit beside fasciculations, paralysis and seizures. **Atropine** blocks muscarinic danger and saves life at titrated doses guided by chest and pupils. **Pralidoxime** reactivates enzyme before ageing and helps nicotinic weakness recover faster. Remove contaminated clothing and protect rescuers because poison persists on skin and garments. Early antidotes decide outcomes more than later supportive care alone.
steps.say: Organophosphates are dangerous because they flood synapses causing pinpoint pupils and salivation together quickly. Bronchospasm and fasciculations and seizures are additional because they complete the picture in poisoning. Atropine is lifesaving because it blocks muscarinic danger and helps breathing recover fast. Oximes are time critical because they reactivate enzyme before ageing closes their window permanently.

rows: Too little drug or worsening disease

steps.tx: The synapse shows **organophosphate** molecules disabling purple acetylcholinesterase while green acetylcholine floods toward muscarinic, nicotinic and central receptors. Insets display **SLUDGE signs**, atropine blocking muscarinic receptors and **pralidoxime** reactivating enzyme before ageing. This one image teaches mechanism, clinical syndrome and both antidotes in sequence. Examiners expect you to separate muscarinic rescue by atropine from nicotinic rescue by oximes without mixing their roles.
steps.say: The synapse shows organophosphate disabling the enzyme that clears acetylcholine. Flooding causes salivation and miosis and bronchospasm together. Atropine blocks muscarinic effects and oximes reactivate enzyme early. Ageing closes the oxime window within hours for many compounds.

steps.tx: Give atropine fast and oximes early, because ageing within hours closes the oxime window for many compounds permanently. **Carbamate poisoning** is shorter and oximes are usually unnecessary for recovery. In anaesthesia, neostigmine reversal pairs with **glycopyrrolate** so heart and glands are shielded while muscle strength returns. That pairing prevents bradycardia and salivation while nicotinic blockade lifts at the junction. Timing and pairing are the two habits examiners reward here.
steps.say: Atropine must be given fast in organophosphate poisoning cases. Oximes work only before ageing closes their window. Carbamate poisoning is briefer and usually needs no oxime. Neostigmine pairs with glycopyrrolate during blockade reversal routinely.
